transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Lately I can’t seem to focus at work—my mind keeps drifting back to everything that could go wrong with my job. It has gotten to the point where it's really hard to get through my daily tasks.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, or do you still find pleasure in things like hobbies, spending time with family, or going out?

I've actually had to pull back from my art workshops and volunteering because I feel too overwhelmed to keep up with them. Even when I try to do things I love, like my photography, my mind quickly drifts back to worrying about work and I just can't enjoy it.
Have you been feeling down or sad most of the day, nearly every day, or do your main struggles mostly involve worry and feeling overwhelmed?

My main struggles are definitely the worry and feeling overwhelmed, rather than feeling sad or down. My mind is constantly looping through worries about our clinic's reorganization, failing at my job, and our finances, and my whole body just feels too tense to relax. It's more of a constant state of being on edge and overwhelmed than feeling depressed.
Do you ever feel physically restless, like you can't sit still or your body feels keyed up, because of your worry?

Yes, I feel constantly revved up inside, like I'm always tapping my foot at my desk, clenching my shoulders, and jumping at every email pop-up. Even when I get home, I can't just sink into the couch because my whole body feels too tense to relax.
Do these physical symptoms of restlessness and tension happen nearly every day, and have they been going on for at least six months?

Yes, I feel this physical tension almost every single day, to the point where I'm constantly clenching my shoulders and can't relax even at home. It has been happening steadily for about nine months now, ever since they first announced the reorganization at the clinic.
